transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Mariana Lopez (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Avalon Head of Platform), Tom Reynolds (Avalon Infra), Sara Kim (Avalon Procurement)
Shared links: 1) Renewal + expansion deck: https://redwood.app/s/avalon-renewal-deck  2) Benchmark spreadsheet: https://redwood.app/s/avalon-bench-2026

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Customer interested in adding APAC region and increasing reserved capacity by ~2.5x for Q1 ramp; discussing pricing delta and 12-month extension discount.
- Security gating items: SOC2 attestation, KMS/HSM key policies, V P C peering details, data residency for EU and APAC.
- Next steps: Redwood to share updated quote, run benchmarks, and draft contract amendment.

Transcript:
[00:00] Mariana: Okay thanks everyone for hopping on. we wanted to run through renewal and expansion options. I know you've had our dedicated pool running for the last six months. Hi Priya, Tom, Sara.
[00:18] Priya: Hey Mariana. Thanks. yeah this is mostly focused on capacity and regions APAC is top of mind for us. we're seeing uptick in japanese and singapore traffic.
[00:28] Ethan: quick note, we'll call out a perf baseline later but initial ask from infra was about a 2x to 3x reserved capacity bump with the ability to burst.
[00:36] Tom: yeah, exactly. currently on Redwood hosted plus a small dedicated pool. our peak p95 latency for live inference is around 520 ms, that's with batch sizes of about 8, qps spikes to ~220.
[00:49] Priya: our product goal is 300 ms p95 by end of Q1 if possible. that will require some routing to lower-latency regions and more dedicated slots.
[00:58] Mariana: got it, thanks. to set expectations, we typically do a blended quote for hosted + dedicated tiers and then show the delta for adding dedicated nodes in additional regions. we'll include APAC (tokyo and singapore) in the quote.
[01:12] Sara: procurement question: if we extend the contract for 12 months, what kind of committed discount can we expect? also need to know invoice cadence and PO requirements.
[01:23] Mariana: totally. for a 12-month extension with a 2.5x capacity commit, we can usually offer a 15% discount on committed usage and a priority scheduling SLA. invoice cadence is flexible monthly or quarterly POs are fine, legal needs a standard MSA amendment. I'll draft language.
[01:38] Tom: on security, we need SOC2 type II and an option for customer-managed keys H S M/KMS. also data residency rules: EU data must stay in EU, APAC in APAC where feasible.
[01:50] Ethan: we support KMS integrations; for private deployments or V P C peering we can surface HSM-backed KMS options. note sometimes the transcript spells VPC as V P C in our notes but that's the same. our private control plane option lets you manage keys and audit logs.
[02:05] Priya: great. also curious about model variants if we need a smaller quantized model for cost efficiency can we fallback gracefully when dedicated is saturated?
[02:15] Ethan: yes we have routing policies and fallback to compatible model variants. sometimes product names in docs show "Redwood Dedi" but it's Redwood Dedicated; the runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching to reduce token cost. small caveat: quantization can impact quality for some prompts, we'll recommend a quick eval set.
[02:33] Mariana: want to dig into perf later; Ethan can run a benchmark with your sample prompt set. we'll want the test corpus and expected throughput/p95 targets.
[02:45] Priya: we'll upload a 10k-query test corpus to the shared spreadsheet, link is above.
[02:52] Tom: curious about multi-region consistency if we add tokyo + singapore, can you guarantee routing policies that keep eu traffic in eu?
[03:01] Ethan: yes, routing by region is supported. we can route by IP geolocation or by the customer's route header; we also support fallbacks to nearest compatible region. there is an inter-region replication for cache meta-data but no raw data movement unless configured.
[03:16] Sara: legal wants to confirm data retention windows and logs for audit. is there an audit log export?
[03:24] Ethan: yes, you can pull audit logs; we also provide per-request telemetry via the Console and can export to your SIEM. retention and export options depend on your plan; Dedicated/Private tiers offer longer retention.
[03:36] Mariana: i'll add SOC2 docs and the audit log export notes to the follow-up.

[10:12] Ethan: jumping ahead to pricing: for the committed capacity increase we typically split charges into reserved hourly node cost + per-token overage. for example, your current dedicated pool is 8 nodes; increasing to 20 nodes for APAC/US/EU split would increase the monthly commit by ~2.5x I'll put numbers in the quote.
[10:31] Tom: how does autoscaling and burst capacity work? we need predictable throughput during batch jobs but don't want to pay for unused headroom.
[10:40] Mariana: we can model an autoscale policy with a baseline reserved capacity and a capped burst that uses on-demand pricing. there's also a burst credit allowance for first 30 minutes of sustained spikes we can discuss.
[10:52] Priya: can Redwood run a short pilot where we provision extra capacity for two weeks and measure real traffic? that helps justify the commit.
[11:01] Mariana: yes we can do a time-boxed pilot; typically there is a small pilot fee or we offset against the commit if you convert. Ethan will scope the pilot runbook.

[18:45] Tom: on the private deployment option, we have one question if we go with Private on-prem in our EU cluster, what's the difference operationally vs Dedicated?
[18:54] Ethan: Private means customer-managed control plane and network isolation; you manage the network, we provide the package or support you through a partner. Dedicated is still hosted by Redwood but with reserved GPU pools in our managed infra; Private gives you full KMS control and on-prem data residency. there can be additional ops overhead and longer lead time.
[19:11] Priya: ops overhead is acceptable if it solves residency and compliance. need cost delta.
[19:16] Mariana: we'll include a quick delta for Private vs Dedicated per region in the quote.

[25:03] Sara: procurement timeline  we need final numbers and the amendment by 12/10 to process payment by year end. is that feasible?
[25:12] Mariana: yes, that's tight but feasible. i'll aim to send the quote and amendment draft by 12/03.
[25:19] Priya: one more technical: can Redwood expose per-route throttles and token-level cost breakdowns in the console for product owners?
[25:28] Ethan: yes, Console has per-route/model dashboards, token breakdowns, and trace hooks. we can enable a role for your product analytics team.

[32:40] Tom: for benchmarks, can we test with our p95 target of 300 ms? what hardware do you run in APAC?
[32:50] Ethan: APAC is on A100-equivalent instances with custom kernels; for low-latency we recommend smaller batch sizes and local region serving. the benchmark will run with the same instance types we propose for production.
[33:04] Priya: any gotchas on quantization? we've seen hallucination regressions with some 4-bit models.
[33:12] Ethan: yes quantization can change outputs. we'll include both recommended quant profiles and quality regression checks tied to your eval set. Redwood Optimize can suggest tradeoffs.

[40:21] Mariana: ok recap before we close: ACTIONS  Mariana send updated quote + amendment draft by 12/03; Ethan run benchmark and share results by 12/07; Priya share p95 targets and test corpus by 12/02; Sara confirm procurement timeline and legal points by 12/10.
[40:41] Sara: confirmed.
[40:44] Priya: sounds good. one ask  can you include a sample SLA with latency SLOs in the quote?
[40:50] Mariana: yes we'll attach a sample SLA and also include the priority scheduling language for committed customers.

[51:10] Mariana: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and pancake the quote in the deck link.
[51:18] Tom: thanks.
[51:20] Sara: bye all.

End of transcript.

Notes about transcription quality: speaker overlaps and some product names may be mis-typed (e.g., Redwood Dedi -> Redwood Dedicated, V P C -> VPC, K V cache -> KV cache).
